beginner.headline: US Citizen Freed by Russia Without a Prisoner Swap
beginner.brief: Russia freed US citizen Stephen Hubbard. Donald Trump said the former teacher was released without any swap required. A US envoy met Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg for talks. Trump later said the man was on his way back home. Trump said he made a request directly to Putin last week. Hubbard was in poor health and needed treatment in Texas.

intermediate.headline: American Released by Russia During Talks in St Petersburg
intermediate.brief: Russia has released a 74-year-old American man who was jailed for allegedly fighting for Ukraine. Stephen Hubbard was sentenced to almost seven years in a penal colony after Russian forces captured him in 2022. President Donald Trump stated that Hubbard was on his way home and that no prisoner exchange was required. This release happened as President Vladimir Putin met with a US representative for talks in St Petersburg. The US government had previously classified the man as wrongfully detained. Reports indicated that Hubbard was in poor health and would travel to Texas for medical care. During the meeting, the US representative also asked Putin to consider restarting peace negotiations with Ukraine. Furthermore, Trump recently suspended some sanctions on Russia, arguing that these penalties would have stopped the talks.

advanced.headline: Russia Releases American Without Conditions Amid Diplomatic Tensions
advanced.brief: Russia has released a 74-year-old American who was jailed for purportedly fighting on behalf of Ukraine. The Russian president confirmed during an early Wednesday meeting that Stephen Hubbard had been transported to Pulkovo Airport. Donald Trump stated that the release followed a direct request he made to the Russian leader last week. He added that the release did not require any reciprocal concessions from the United States. American news outlets reported that the elderly man was in poor health and expected to be flown to Texas for medical care. Trump defended his move to pause impending sanctions against Russia, arguing that enforcing them would have brought diplomatic discussions to a complete halt. Steve Witkoff thanked Putin for a deal struck with Washington earlier this month to import Russian diesel. This diesel agreement infuriated Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, triggering a tumultuous period of deteriorating relations. Witkoff also urged Putin to consider resuming trilateral peace talks, seeking an end to a conflict that grinds on into its fifth year. Meanwhile, Kyiv accused Washington of withholding vital intelligence, a claim the US firmly rejected as scandalous. However, Zelensky confirmed that intelligence sharing had resumed after constructive talks with American officials in Oslo.
